mainTopic: The status of a newborn who might be a נפל: מילה on שבת, a בן שמונה animal, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's waiting period, mourning, and יבום
overview: The גמרא has learned that a newborn is not proven viable until it lives a set time, so it asks how we can do a ברית מילה on שבת. רב אדא בר אהבה answers with ממה נפשך: either the מילה is a מצוה, or the person is only cutting dead flesh. A ברייתא seems to forbid this for a baby who may be a בן שמונה. The גמרא answers that the ברייתא forbids only the preparations (מכשירי מילה), following רבי אליעזר. אביי links the question to a dispute among תנאים about slaughtering a בן שמונה animal. רבא rejects the link and explains that dispute as an argument over comparing the animal to a טרפה. The גמרא then proves from שמואל that the רבנן disagree with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and that the הלכה follows him. After defining exactly which deaths are disputed, two stories show that a baby known to be full-term is mourned even if it died within thirty days. The amud ends with a new case of a widow who got engaged before the יבום question was settled, and the ruling continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How can we circumcise on שבת if the baby might be non-viable?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how מילה can be done on שבת if every baby under thirty days might be a נפל.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, as for circumcision, how can we circumcise him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem with what it just learned. If a baby under thirty days might be a נפל, how can we circumcise him on שבת?
steps.deeperAnalysis: מילה overrides שבת only for a real, living Jewish baby. If the baby might be a נפל, then maybe there is no מצוה at all. In that case the cutting would just be a forbidden wound on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: a non-viable baby, considered as if never truly alive

steps.confusionAlert: This line connects to the previous discussion, which said a baby is not proven viable until thirty days. Without that background, the question makes no sense.

phrases.english: Circumcision — how can we circumcise him?!
phrases.notes: The baby might be a נפל, so maybe there is no מצוה that could override שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִימְהָל הֵיכִי מָהֲלִינַן לֵיהּ
steps.kashyaTarget: The practice of circumcising on שבת on the eighth day
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If every baby under thirty days is in doubt of being a נפל, then the מצוה might not exist. Without a sure מצוה, cutting on שבת should be forbidden.

steps.title: Either way, circumcising is allowed
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה answers that we may circumcise because of ממה נפשך: either it is a מצוה, or it is only cutting dead flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: We circumcise him no matter which way you look at it. If he is alive, the circumcision is proper. If not, the person is just cutting flesh.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה shows that circumcising is fine whichever way the doubt turns out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the baby is viable, the מילה is a מצוה that overrides שבת. If he is a נפל, he has the status of a dead body. Cutting dead flesh is not the מלאכה of making a wound. Since neither possibility involves a forbidden act, we may circumcise.

keyTerms.meaning: whichever way you look at it; both sides of the doubt lead to the same result
merely cutting flesh (of a dead body, which is not a forbidden wound)

steps.whyThisMatters: The ממה נפשך method shows up often in the גמרא. When every side of a doubt is permitted, the doubt does not matter.

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
We circumcise him, whichever way you look at it:

phrases.aramaic: אִם חַי הוּא — שַׁפִּיר קָא מָהֵיל,
phrases.english: If he is a living (viable) child — he is circumcising properly,
and if not — he is merely cutting flesh.
phrases.notes: Cutting a dead body is not considered making a wound on שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: מָלִין אוֹתוֹ מִמָּה נַפְשָׁךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: ממה נפשך: both sides of the doubt are permitted
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the doubt about a נפל made the מילה a possible violation of שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: No possibility involves a forbidden act, so we may circumcise.

steps.title: A ברייתא forbids desecrating שבת for a doubtful eighth-month baby
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that we do not desecrate שבת for a baby who may be a בן שמונה. Why not apply ממה נפשך there too?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, what about the ברייתא that teaches: if there is doubt whether he is a seven-month baby or an eight-month baby, we do not desecrate שבת for him. Why not? Let us circumcise him, whichever way you look at it! If he is alive, the circumcision is proper, and if not, he is just cutting flesh!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אדא בר אהבה with a ברייתא that seems to forbid circumcising a doubtful baby on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the גמרא's view, a seven-month baby is viable but an eight-month baby is not. A baby in doubt between the two is the same kind of doubt רב אדא handled. Yet the ברייתא says not to desecrate שבת for him. So his ממה נפשך reasoning seems to be contradicted.

keyTerms.meaning: that was taught in a ברייתא
a baby born in the seventh month (viable)
a baby born in the eighth month (considered non-viable)

phrases.english: But then, that which was taught in a Baraita:

phrases.aramaic: סָפֵק בֶּן שִׁבְעָה, סָפֵק בֶּן שְׁמוֹנָה —
phrases.english: If it is uncertain whether he is a seven-month baby or an eight-month baby —
we do not desecrate Shabbat on his behalf,
Why? Let us circumcise him, whichever way you look at it!

phrases.aramaic: אִם חַי הוּא — שַׁפִּיר קָא מָהֵיל,
phrases.english: If he is alive — he is circumcising properly,
and if not — he is merely cutting flesh!
phrases.notes: The גמרא repeats רב אדא's own words to turn them against the ברייתא.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא הָא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ממה נפשך answer of step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אדא בר אהבה's ממה נפשך permission
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא forbids desecrating שבת for a doubtful baby. The same ממה נפשך reasoning should have permitted it.

steps.title: The ברייתא refers only to preparations for circumcision, following רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: מר בריה דרבינא explains that the cutting itself is permitted. The ברייתא only forbids מכשירי מילה, according to רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר, the son of רבינא, said: I and רב נחומי בר זכריה explained it this way. As for the circumcision itself, we do indeed circumcise him. The ברייתא was needed only for the preparations for circumcision, and it follows the view of רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: מר בריה דרבינא answers the challenge. The ברייתא was never talking about the cutting itself, only about the preparations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that preparations for מילה, like bringing the knife through the public domain, override שבת. For a doubtful baby, ממה נפשך does not work for those preparations. Carrying the knife is a real מלאכה even if the baby turns out to be a נפל. So the ברייתא forbids the preparations, while the cutting stays permitted, just as רב אדא said.

keyTerms.meaning: it was only needed for (narrows the case)
preparations for circumcision, such as bringing or making the knife
according to the opinion of רבי אליעזר

steps.whatToRemember: A doubtful baby may be circumcised on שבת because of ממה נפשך. But preparations like carrying the knife are forbidden, because they are a real מלאכה whichever way the doubt turns out. That is the limit of the ברייתא, according to רבי אליעזר.
steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא's phrase אין מחללין does not forbid the מילה itself. It only rules out the extra שבת-violating preparations, which רבי אליעזר would normally allow.

phrases.english: Mar, son of Ravina, said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲנָא וְרַב נְחוּמִי בַּר זְכַרְיָה תַּרְגֵּימְנָא:
phrases.english: I and Rav Nachumi bar Zecharya explained it:
Circumcision — indeed, we do circumcise him.
It was needed only for the preparations of circumcision,
phrases.notes: For example, carrying the knife or making it on שבת.

phrases.english: and according to Rabbi Eliezer.
phrases.notes: רבי אליעזר normally lets preparations override שבת, so the ברייתא teaches that this does not apply to a doubtful baby.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבִינָא: אֲנָא וְרַב נְחוּמִי בַּר זְכַרְיָה תַּרְגֵּימְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3 by narrowing the ברייתא's case
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) to מכשירי מילה, according to רבי אליעזר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to forbid the מילה itself for a doubtful baby.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מילה is permitted by ממה נפשך. Only the preparations are forbidden, since they are real מלאכה whichever way the doubt turns out.

steps.title: אביי links the question to a dispute among the תנאים
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the status of a doubtful-viability newborn matches a dispute among תנאים about a בן שמונה animal. The ברייתא learns from a פסוק that its שחיטה does not purify it. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון say it does.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: this matches a dispute among the תנאים. The verse says 'And if any animal that is yours to eat shall die.' This comes to include a בן שמונה, an animal born after only eight months, whose שחיטה does not make it טהור. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון say: its שחיטה does make it טהור.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a ברייתא with a dispute about slaughtering an animal born after eight months. He claims it is the same question we have been asking about doubtful newborns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An unslaughtered dead animal (נבלה) makes people טמא, but proper שחיטה prevents that. The first opinion says שחיטה does not help a בן שמונה, so it is still a נבלה. The two תנאים, רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, disagree and say שחיטה does help.

keyTerms.meaning: It is like (parallel to) a dispute among the Tannaim
One born after only eight months of pregnancy, considered unable to survive
Purifies it, so it does not carry נבלה impurity
To include (a derivation from a פסוק)

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'purify' does not mean the animal may be eaten. It only means the slaughtered body does not make people טמא like a נבלה.

phrases.english: Abaye said: this is like a dispute of the Tannaim:
"And if any of the animals shall die
that are yours for eating"
this comes to include an eight-month-born animal
whose slaughter does not purify it.
Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda
and Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon say:
its slaughter purifies it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, כְּתַנָּאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new line: the question of a בן שמונה's status is traced back to a dispute among תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a dispute among תנאים over whether שחיטה purifies a בן שמונה animal.

steps.title: Suggesting the dispute is about alive versus dead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that the תנאים argue over whether a בן שמונה counts as alive, so שחיטה works, or as dead, so שחיטה does nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this what they argue about? One master holds it counts as alive, and the other master holds it counts as dead.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why אביי called this a dispute among תנאים. It suggests the two sides argue about whether a בן שמונה counts as a living creature.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If it counts as alive, שחיטה works on it like on any animal. If it already counts as dead, slaughtering it is like cutting a corpse, so it stays a נבלה. This would make the ברייתא a direct source for our question about newborns.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not that...? (introduces a suggested reading)

phrases.english: Is it not about this that they disagree:
that one master holds it is alive,
and the other master holds it is dead.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לָאו בְּהָא קָא מִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind אביי's comparison.
steps.raayaObject: That a בן שמונה's status as alive or dead is debated among תנאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about שחיטה purifying a בן שמונה animal.

steps.title: רבא: then they should have argued about eating
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects. If the argument were alive versus dead, the sides should have argued about the bigger issue, whether the animal may be eaten, rather than only about impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: if so, instead of arguing about impurity and purity, let them argue about eating!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the reading from the last step. If the argument were really about alive versus dead, the תנאים would have argued about whether the animal may be eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a בן שמונה counted as alive, its שחיטה would make it fully kosher to eat. Yet the ברייתא only discusses impurity, which suggests everyone agrees it may not be eaten. So the argument must be about something else.

phrases.english: Rava said: if so,
instead of disagreeing about impurity and purity,
let them disagree about eating!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אִי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggested explanation of the dispute.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the תנאים argue over whether a בן שמונה is alive or dead.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An alive-versus-dead argument would show up mainly as an argument about eating, but the ברייתא only discusses impurity.

steps.title: Everyone agrees it is dead; the argument is about comparing it to a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees a בן שמונה counts as dead. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון compare it to a טרפה, whose שחיטה still saves it from impurity. The רבנן reject the comparison because a טרפה once had a time of fitness and a בן שמונה never did.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, everyone agrees it counts as dead. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון hold that it is like a טרפה. Even though a טרפה counts as dead, doesn't its שחיטה make it טהור? Here too, it is no different. The רבנן say it is not like a טרפה. A טרפה once had a time when it was fit. This animal never had a time when it was fit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new explanation of the dispute. Both sides agree the animal counts as dead. They argue only about whether it can be compared to a טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טרפה is a fatally injured animal. It is forbidden to eat, but its שחיטה still prevents נבלה impurity. One side applies the same rule to a בן שמונה. The רבנן say a טרפה was once healthy and fit, while a בן שמונה was never fit for even a moment, so שחיטה cannot help it. Since both sides agree it is dead, אביי's link to our question falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a fatal defect; it may not be eaten
A time of fitness, a period when it was once valid

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, everyone agrees a בן שמונה counts as dead. The argument is only whether it is like a טרפה. One side says yes, so שחיטה purifies it. The רבנן say no, because it never had a שעת הכושר.
steps.confusionAlert: Calling a טרפה 'dead' is a legal label for an animal that cannot survive. It is not literally dead, which is why שחיטה can still work on it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This removes the ברייתא as proof that the alive-or-dead status of a doubtful newborn is a dispute among תנאים. It also introduces the idea that having once had a שעת הכושר can affect a halachic outcome.

phrases.english: Rather, everyone agrees it is dead,
and Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבְרִי כִּטְרֵפָה:
phrases.english: and Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon hold it is like a treifa:

phrases.aramaic: טְרֵפָה לָאו אַף עַל גַּב דְּמֵתָה הִיא —
phrases.english: a treifa, is it not that even though it is considered dead,
its slaughter purifies it?
Here too, it is no different.
And the Rabbis: it is not similar to a treifa,
a treifa had a time of fitness,

phrases.aramaic: הַאי — לֹא הָיְתָה לָהּ שְׁעַת הַכּוֹשֶׁר.
phrases.english: this one never had a time of fitness.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא מֵת הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the alive-versus-dead reading, רבא offers a new explanation of the dispute.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנאים argue whether a בן שמונה is alive or dead.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone agrees it is dead. They argue only whether it can be compared to a טרפה, which once had a שעת הכושר.

steps.title: What about an animal that was a טרפה from birth?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the רבנן's distinction. A טרפה from the womb never had a time of fitness either, yet its שחיטה still works.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: what about an animal that was a טרפה from the womb? What can be said about that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reason the רבנן just gave in Step 8. Some טרפה animals were born that way and never had a time of fitness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 8 the רבנן said a טרפה is different from a בן שמונה because a טרפה once had a time of fitness. But a טרפה מבטן was damaged from birth and never had such a time. Yet its שחיטה still protects it from impurity, so the distinction seems to fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a possible objection)
An animal with a fatal defect from the womb

phrases.english: And if you will say:
a טרפה from the womb,
what is there to say?
phrases.notes: It never had a time of fitness, yet its שחיטה works.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: טְרֵפָה מִבֶּטֶן, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the רבנן's reason given in Step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's claim that a טרפה differs because it once had a time of fitness
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A טרפה מבטן never had a time of fitness, but its שחיטה still works. So that cannot be the real difference.

steps.title: A טרפה belongs to a type that can be slaughtered
steps.stepSummary: The difference is the type of animal. Animals of a טרפה's type are normally slaughtered, but a בן שמונה's type is never fit for שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, with a טרפה, its type has שחיטה. Here, with a בן שמונה, its type has no שחיטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by changing the reason. The question is no longer about this one animal's history. It is about its type.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a טרפה from birth belongs to a group, regular animals, where שחיטה works. A בן שמונה belongs to a group that is treated as dead, so no animal of that type is ever fit for שחיטה. This keeps the רבנן's position standing.

keyTerms.meaning: Here (the case of the בן שמונה)
Its type is subject to שחיטה

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן's final distinction is about the type of animal: a טרפה's type can be slaughtered, and a בן שמונה's type never can.

phrases.english: There, its type has slaughter;
here, its type has no slaughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם — יֵשׁ בְּמִינָהּ שְׁחִיטָה, הָכָא — אֵין בְּמִינָהּ שְׁחִיטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Refined distinction (from the animal's own history to the type of animal)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference depends on whether this animal ever had a time of fitness
steps.terutzMaskana: The difference depends on whether the animal's type is fit for שחיטה

steps.title: Do the רבנן disagree with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and whose view is the הלכה?
steps.stepSummary: A two-part question is raised. Do the רבנן argue with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's eight-day rule? If they do, is the הלכה like him?
steps.simpleTranslation: It was asked of them: do the רבנן disagree with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל or not? And if you say they disagree, is the הלכה like him or not like him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's rule. That rule says an animal is not known to be viable until it has lived eight days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part asks whether there is any argument at all. The second part asks, if there is an argument, which side the הלכה follows. The practical issue is whether a newborn animal may be slaughtered before eight days.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them
If you will say (the second stage of a question)

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
Do the Rabbis disagree

phrases.aramaic: עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, אוֹ לָא?
phrases.english: with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, or not?
phrases.notes: He holds that an animal is only established as viable after eight days.

phrases.english: If you say they disagree,
is the halakha like him,
or is the halakha not like him?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מִי פְּלִיגִי רַבָּנַן עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's eight-day rule
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether there is a dispute with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and if so, whether the הלכה follows him

steps.title: Proof from a calf born on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: A source says a calf born on יום טוב may be slaughtered that same day. This seems to ignore the eight-day wait.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: a calf that was born on יום טוב may be slaughtered on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to try to answer the question. It shows that a calf may be slaughtered on the day it is born.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we had to wait eight days to know an animal is viable, it could not be slaughtered on the day of its birth. Since this source allows it, either the רבנן disagree with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, or the הלכה is not like him.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
a calf that was born on a Festival,
one may slaughter it on the Festival!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: עֵגֶל שֶׁנּוֹלַד בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attempts to answer the question of Step 11
steps.raayaObject: That the eight-day wait is not accepted
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling that a calf born on יום טוב may be slaughtered that day

steps.title: The calf is known to be full-term
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The case may be one where we know for sure the calf completed its full pregnancy.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? One where he is certain that its months of pregnancy were completed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof by limiting the case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even רבן שמעון בן גמליאל only requires eight days when we are unsure the animal is viable. If we know the calf finished its full months, there is no doubt at all. So the source does not show that anyone argues with him.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (limits the case)

steps.confusionAlert: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's eight days is not an absolute rule for every newborn. It only applies when we don't know whether the pregnancy was full-term.

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
Where one is certain about it
that its months were completed.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן, דְּקִים לֵיהּ בְּגַוֵּויהּ שֶׁכָּלוּ לוֹ חֳדָשָׁיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 12
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The source can be read as a case of a known full-term calf, where even רבן שמעון בן גמליאל agrees

steps.title: Proof from a בכור born with a blemish
steps.stepSummary: A second source says everyone agrees a בכור born with its blemish counts as prepared for יום טוב. This implies it may be slaughtered the day it is born.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: and they agree that if it was born together with its blemish, it counts as prepared.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second proof. It comes from the case of a firstborn animal born with a blemish on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון argue about checking a בכור for blemishes on יום טוב. They agree that one born with a blemish is מוכן, ready for use that day. That means it can be slaughtered on its birthday, again seeming to ignore the eight-day wait.

keyTerms.meaning: Blemish (which lets a בכור be slaughtered outside the Temple)
Counts as prepared (permitted for use on יום טוב)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
And they agree that if it was born
it and its blemish with it,
this is from the prepared!
phrases.notes: So it may be slaughtered on the day of its birth.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: וְשָׁוִין, שֶׁאִם נוֹלַד הוּא וּמוּמוֹ עִמּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second attempt to answer Step 11 after the first proof failed
steps.raayaObject: That a newborn may be slaughtered without waiting eight days
steps.raayaSupportSource: The agreement of רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון about a בכור born with its blemish

steps.title: This too is a full-term animal
steps.stepSummary: The second proof is rejected the same way. The case may be one where the animal is known to have completed its months.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it is a case where its months were completed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the second proof with the same answer it gave before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בכור can also be read as a case where we know the pregnancy was full-term, so there is no doubt about its viability. So this proof does not answer the question of Step 11. The next proof, in Steps 16-17, answers it.
steps.whatToRemember: Both proofs fail for the same reason. A known full-term animal may be slaughtered right away according to everyone, so neither source settles the question about רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

phrases.english: Here too,
it is where its months were completed.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי שֶׁכָּלוּ לוֹ חֳדָשָׁיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 14 using the same answer as Step 13
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case can be read as a known full-term animal

steps.title: שמואל rules like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רב יהודה quoting שמואל: the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל, 'The הלכה is like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.'
steps.whatsHappening: After two failed proofs, the גמרא brings a new source to answer the question from step 11. שמואל rules that the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This statement directly answers the second half of the question: yes, the הלכה is like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. In the next line, the גמרא will show that it also answers the first half.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the formula that introduces a proof
The final practical law follows the opinion of...
The תנא who requires a waiting period (eight days for an animal) before we know a newborn is viable

phrases.english: Come and hear,
as Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third proof attempt, after the first two were rejected in steps 13 and 15.
steps.raayaObject: That the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and that the רבנן disagree with him

steps.title: A ruling of הלכה proves there is an argument
steps.stepSummary: Saying 'the הלכה is like him' implies that someone disagrees. So both parts of the question are answered.
steps.simpleTranslation: If שמואל had to say 'the הלכה is like him,' that implies the רבנן argue. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that שמואל would only need to rule if there were an argument. So the statement answers both questions at once, and the גמרא closes the inquiry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one rules 'the הלכה is like X' about an opinion nobody disputes. The ruling itself therefore proves the רבנן argue, which answers part one. The ruling's content answers part two.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it: the question is resolved

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן do argue with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. A newborn is not considered definitely viable until its waiting period passes.

phrases.english: 'Halakha' — by inference, they disagree.
Conclude from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲלָכָה מִכְּלָל דִּפְלִיגִי שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the full conclusion from שמואל's ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The רבנן disagree with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: אביי defines exactly where they argue
steps.stepSummary: אביי says a baby killed by an accident is agreed to have been alive. The argument is only about a baby that breathed and then died on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: If a baby fell from a roof or a lion ate it, everyone agrees it was a living baby. They only argue when the baby yawned (took a breath) and died. One side holds it counts as alive, and the other side holds it counts as dead (a נפל).
steps.whatsHappening: אביי narrows the argument between רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and the רבנן about a baby less than 30 days old. He tells us which case is agreed on and which case is disputed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An outside cause of death, like a fall or a lion, means the baby did not die from weakness, so all agree it was viable. When the baby dies by itself right after birth, the רבנן say it was born alive. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says it is treated as a נפל because it did not reach 30 days.

keyTerms.meaning: Fell off the roof (an outside, accidental death)
A non-viable newborn, treated as if never truly alive

steps.confusionAlert: 'מר סבר חי הוא' refers to the רבנן, and 'מר סבר מת הוא' refers to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who requires 30 days for a person.

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: נָפַל מִן הַגָּג אוֹ אֲכָלוֹ אֲרִי —
phrases.english: If it fell off a roof or a lion ate it —
everyone agrees it was alive.
Where they disagree is when it yawned and died.
One master holds: it was alive,
and the other master holds: it was dead.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי נָפַל מִן הַגָּג אוֹ אֲכָלוֹ אֲרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that we know they argue, אביי defines the scope of the argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An accidental death proves the baby was viable according to everyone. The dispute is only about a baby that breathed and died naturally.

steps.title: What difference does it make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference it makes whether such a baby counts as alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: What practical difference is there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the practical result of אביי's distinction. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The baby has already died either way, so it is not obvious what changes. The גמרא wants a real halachic consequence.

phrases.english: What practical difference is there?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאי נָפְקָא מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the practical result of אביי's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The halachic consequence of whether the baby counts as having lived

steps.title: The difference is יבום
steps.stepSummary: If the baby counts as alive, the father left a child, so the widow is exempt from יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: To exempt the mother from יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the difference concerns יבום. A widow whose husband left a living child does not need יבום or חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the baby counts as alive, even briefly, the husband did not die childless, and the widow is exempt. If the baby is a נפל, he died childless, and she needs יבום or חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Levirate marriage: the brother marries the widow of a man who died childless

phrases.english: To exempt from levirate marriage.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִפְטוֹר מִן הַיִּיבּוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Whether the widow is exempt from יבום

steps.title: A story about a calf slaughtered on its seventh day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי's claim that an accidental death proves viability. רב פפא and רב הונא refused to eat a calf slaughtered on day seven.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it really agreed that if the baby fell off a roof or a lion ate it, it was alive? But רב פפא and רב הונא son of רב יהושע visited the house of the son of רב אידי בר אבין. He prepared them a choice calf on its seventh day. They told him: 'Had you waited until evening, we would have eaten from it. Now we will not eat from it!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי with a story. Two אמוראים would not eat a calf slaughtered before its eighth day, even though slaughtering is an outside cause of death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slaughtering kills the calf from the outside, just like a fall or a lion. Even so, the rabbis still treated the calf as a possible נפל because its eight days were not complete. That suggests an accidental death does not prove viability, which contradicts אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: A choice calf (explained as a third-born or one-third-grown calf)

steps.whyThisMatters: It tests whether an outside cause of death can ever prove viability before the waiting period ends. This matters for both animals and people.

phrases.aramaic: נָפַל מִן הַגָּג אוֹ אֲכָלוֹ אֲרִי —
phrases.english: If it fell off a roof or a lion ate it —
does everyone agree it was alive?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַב פָּפָּא וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: But Rav Pappa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua

phrases.aramaic: אִיקְּלַעוּ לְבֵי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין,
phrases.english: happened to come to the house of the son of Rav Idi bar Avin,
and they prepared for them a choice calf
on the seventh day.
And they said to him:
Had you waited with it until evening —
we would have eaten from it;
now — we will not eat from it!

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפַל מִן הַגָּג אוֹ אֲכָלוֹ אֲרִי דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל חַי הוּא וְהָא רַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the first half of אביי's statement in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that everyone agrees an accidental death proves the newborn was alive
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A calf slaughtered (an outside death) on day seven was still treated as a possible נפל. So an outside death does not prove viability before the waiting period ends.

steps.title: אביי's statement is reversed
steps.stepSummary: After the challenge, אביי's statement is rewritten. A baby that dies on its own is agreed to be a נפל. The argument is about a baby killed by an outside accident.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, change it around: if the baby yawned and died, everyone agrees it counts as dead from the start (a נפל). They argue only when it fell off a roof or a lion ate it. One master (רבן שמעון בן גמליאל) holds it still counts as dead. The other master holds it counts as alive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 21 by flipping אביי's statement around. Now the 'agreed' case and the 'argued' case switch places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, אביי said an accidental death clearly proves the baby was viable. רב פפא and רב הונא would not eat a calf slaughtered on day seven, which shows an outside death does not prove viability. So now a natural death is the clear case: everyone agrees it is a נפל. The argument moves to accidental deaths: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל still treats the baby as a נפל, and the חכמים treat it as alive.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather — signals that the earlier version is being replaced
Yawned — here, died on its own with no outside cause

steps.confusionAlert: This is the opposite of אביי's first version in step 18. There, an accidental death was the agreed case. Now a natural death is the agreed case, and the accidental death is the one they argue about.

phrases.english: Rather:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is taking back what it just said and putting it a new way.

phrases.english: when it yawned and died
all agree it is considered dead
where they disagree is when it fell off a roof
or a lion ate it
one master holds: it is considered dead
and the other master holds: it is considered alive

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא כשפיהק ומת דברי הכל מת הוא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 21 by reversing אביי's statement
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rewriting the statement (reversing which case is agreed and which is argued)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An accidental death proves the baby was viable, so everyone agrees it was alive
steps.terutzMaskana: A natural death is agreed to be a נפל. An accidental death is argued: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says it is a נפל, and the חכמים say it was alive

steps.title: רב דימי's son mourns a baby who died within thirty days
steps.stepSummary: The son of רב דימי בר יוסף mourned a baby who died within thirty days. He explained that he knew for sure the baby was born full-term.
steps.simpleTranslation: A baby was born to the son of רב דימי בר יוסף, and it died within thirty days. The son sat and mourned over it. His father said to him: 'Do you want to eat the mourners' delicacies?' He answered: 'I know for sure that the baby was born full-term.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about a father who mourned a baby who died before thirty days. His own father questioned why he was mourning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: a baby who dies before thirty days may be a נפל, and we do not mourn a נפל. So the grandfather pointedly challenges him: is he mourning only to get the mourners' food? The son answers that the thirty-day rule is only for when we are unsure. If we know the full nine months were completed, the baby is not a נפל, and he must be mourned.

keyTerms.meaning: Its months of pregnancy were completed (born full-term)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule: the thirty-day test only applies when we are unsure. If the baby is known to be full-term, it is not a נפל, even if it died early.

phrases.english: The son of Rav Dimi bar Yosef
had a certain baby born to him.
Within thirty days it died.
He sat mourning over it.
His father said to him:
Do you want to eat delicacies?
phrases.notes: Meaning: are you mourning just for the mourners' meal? A נפל is not mourned

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: קִים לִי בֵּיהּ שֶׁכָּלוּ לוֹ חֳדָשָׁיו.
phrases.english: I know for certain about it that its months were completed.

steps.triggerLanguage: בריה דרב דימי בר יוסף איתיליד ליה ההוא ינוקא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the theory of נפל to a real-life case of mourning
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A baby known to be full-term is mourned, even if it died within thirty days

steps.title: רב כהנא mourns, and רב אשי questions him
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי saw רב כהנא mourning a baby who died within thirty days. He asked about the ruling that the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. רב כהנא answered that he knew the baby was full-term.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי came to the house of רב כהנא. A sad thing happened to רב כהנא: his baby died within thirty days. רב אשי saw him sitting and mourning over it. He said to him: 'Don't you hold what רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל, that the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל?' He answered: 'I know for sure that the baby was born full-term.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second story makes the same point. This time the question openly mentions the ruling of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי asks a direct legal question: since the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, a baby who dies before thirty days is treated as a נפל and not mourned. רב כהנא gives the same answer as in the first story. Knowing the baby was full-term overrides the thirty-day test.

keyTerms.meaning: A bad thing happened to him (a gentle way to say someone died)

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: a baby who dies within thirty days is treated as a נפל. But if it is known for sure that the baby was full-term, it is not a נפל, and we mourn it.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָשֵׁי אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רַב כָּהֲנָא.
phrases.english: Rav Ashi happened to come to Rav Kahana's house.
A sad thing befell him
within thirty days.
He saw him sitting and mourning over it.
He said to him:
Doesn't the master hold this
that Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
The halacha follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel?
He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: קִים לִי בְּגַוֵּיהּ שֶׁכָּלוּ לוֹ חֳדָשָׁיו.
phrases.english: I know for certain about it that its months were completed.

steps.triggerLanguage: רב אשי איקלע לבי רב כהנא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story that repeats and strengthens the point of step 23
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even though the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, a baby known to be full-term is mourned

steps.title: New case: the widow got engaged before the case was decided
steps.stepSummary: A new case is set up. A baby died within thirty days, and its mother went ahead and got engaged to another man. רבינא is about to rule in the name of רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: a baby died within thirty days, and the mother went ahead and got engaged. רבינא said in the name of רבא:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new question. The answer from רבינא in the name of רבא comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the baby died within thirty days, we are unsure if it was a נפל. If it was a נפל, the father left no child, and the widow might need יבום or חליצה. She did not wait for a ruling and got engaged to another man. The question is what happens to her now.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (introduces a ruling by the אמוראים)

phrases.english: It was stated:
If the baby died within thirty days,
and she went ahead and became engaged.
phrases.notes: To another man, before the יבום question was settled

phrases.english: Ravina said in the name of Rava:
phrases.notes: His ruling continues on the next amud

steps.triggerLanguage: איתמר מת בתוך שלשים ועמדה ונתקדשה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from mourning back to the יבום issue raised in step 20
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup only. רבינא's ruling in the name of רבא comes on the next amud
